title: Apache Kafka Event Streaming
description: Production Apache Kafka reference covering brokers, KRaft, topics, partitions, replication, producers, consumers, offsets, delivery semantics, transactions, schemas, Kafka Streams, Connect, security, capacity, observability, failure recovery, and operations.

subtopics.title: Brokers, KRaft Controllers & Cluster Metadata
subtopics.description: Brokers store and serve partitions; KRaft controllers manage metadata through a replicated quorum. Separate client availability from controller-quorum health and broker storage health.

diagram.content:
flowchart LR
  P["Producers"] --> B1["Broker: partition leaders"]
  B1 <--> B2["Broker: followers/leaders"]
  B2 <--> B3["Broker: followers/leaders"]
  C["KRaft controller quorum"] --> B1
  C --> B2
  C --> B3
  B1 --> G["Consumer groups"]

callouts.title: Controller Quorum Is Not a Data Replica Set
callouts.text: Controllers replicate cluster metadata; topic partitions replicate record data across brokers according to each topic's replication settings.

subtopics.title: Topics, Partitions, Keys & Ordering
subtopics.description: A topic is divided into ordered append-only partitions. A key commonly selects a partition, so ordering is guaranteed only within one partition.

codeBlocks.code:
topic: orders
partition 0: offset 0,1,2,...  keys customer-7, customer-7
partition 1: offset 0,1,2,...  keys customer-9, customer-9

Choose key = unit requiring order and locality
Choose partition count = throughput + parallelism + future scaling tradeoff

callouts.title: Changing Partition Count Can Change Key Placement
callouts.text: Existing records do not move, but future key-to-partition mapping may change. Do not assume lifelong per-key order across repartitioning without an explicit strategy.

subtopics.title: Replication, Retention & Log Compaction
subtopics.description: Leaders handle reads/writes while replicas follow. Retention removes old segments by time/size; compaction retains the latest value per key while tombstones represent deletion.

callouts.title: Compaction Is Asynchronous
callouts.text: Older values and tombstones may remain until cleaning. Consumers must tolerate duplicates and historical versions and must not treat compaction as immediate deletion compliance.

subtopics.title: Producer Batching, acks & Idempotence
subtopics.description: Producer throughput comes from batching and compression; durability depends on acknowledgements, in-sync replicas, retries, and broker/topic configuration. Idempotent producers prevent retry duplicates within supported sessions.

codeBlocks.code:
acks=all
enable.idempotence=true
compression.type=zstd
linger.ms=5
batch.size=65536
delivery.timeout.ms=120000

callouts.title: acks=all Depends on min.insync.replicas
callouts.text: Durable acknowledgement requires enough in-sync replicas and unclean leader election policy aligned with data-loss tolerance. Test broker failure, not just successful sends.

subtopics.title: Consumer Groups, Rebalancing & Offsets
subtopics.description: Within a group, each partition is assigned to at most one consumer at a time. Offsets record progress, not completion of external side effects unless commits are coordinated.

codeBlocks.code:
poll records → process → commit offset after durable effect
max.poll.interval.ms must exceed bounded processing time
cooperative assignment reduces disruptive movement
static membership may reduce churn but needs lifecycle discipline

callouts.title: Disable Auto-Commit for Nontrivial Processing
callouts.text: Time-based automatic commits can advance past unfinished work. Define batch boundaries, retries, poison records, shutdown, and rebalance callbacks deliberately.

subtopics.title: At-Most-Once, At-Least-Once & Transactions
subtopics.description: Delivery semantics describe where progress is recorded relative to effects. Kafka transactions can atomically publish records and consumed offsets within Kafka, but not arbitrary external database effects.

callouts.title: Exactly-Once Is a System Property
callouts.text: External APIs, email, payments, and databases still need idempotency, deduplication, outbox/inbox, or transactional integration. A Kafka setting cannot make every side effect exactly once.

subtopics.title: Serialization & Schema Evolution
subtopics.description: Use a governed schema format and compatibility policy. Producers and consumers deploy independently, so defaults, field presence, enums, and unknown fields must evolve safely.

codeBlocks.code:
Envelope metadata: event ID, event type, schema version, occurred_at, producer
Payload: domain facts, stable identifiers, explicit units/time zones
Compatibility: test old consumer/new producer and new consumer/old data
Registry: authenticate, authorize subjects, back up and monitor

callouts.title: Do Not Put Java Class Names on the Wire
callouts.text: Language/runtime serialization couples consumers to implementation and creates security risk. Use explicit Avro, Protobuf, JSON Schema, or another governed contract.

subtopics.title: Kafka Streams, State Stores & Repartitioning
subtopics.description: Kafka Streams builds processing topologies with tables, streams, windows, joins, changelogs, and repartition topics. Keys and timestamp semantics determine correctness.

codeBlocks.code:
KStream: event stream with independent records
KTable: latest value per key / changelog view
State store: local materialization backed by changelog
Repartition: reshuffle by new key before key-based aggregation/join
Window: event-time grouping + grace for late records

callouts.title: State Recovery Needs Capacity
callouts.text: Plan changelog retention, restoration bandwidth, standby replicas, local disk, rebalance duration, and deployment concurrency for stateful applications.

subtopics.title: Kafka Connect, Sources & Sinks
subtopics.description: Connect workers run connectors composed of tasks. Distributed mode coordinates configuration, offsets, and status through internal topics; connector semantics depend on the external system.

callouts.title: Dead-Letter Queues Need Ownership
callouts.text: Routing failures aside can silently lose business processing. Define alerting, retention, sensitive-data controls, diagnosis, replay, and completion criteria.

subtopics.title: TLS, Authentication & Authorization
subtopics.description: Encrypt client and inter-broker traffic, use supported SASL or mutual TLS identities, authorize topics/groups/transactional IDs, and rotate credentials without outages.

codeBlocks.code:
Client identity → authenticate (mTLS/SASL)
ACL/policy → topic read/write/create + consumer group + transactional ID
Network → private listeners and restricted administration
Secrets → managed distribution, overlap rotation, no logs/config repositories

callouts.title: Topic ACLs Alone Are Incomplete
callouts.text: Consumer group and transactional-ID permissions, admin APIs, schema registry, Connect, monitoring endpoints, and platform/operator access also require protection.

subtopics.title: Capacity, Lag & Observability
subtopics.description: Model bytes in/out, records, partitions, replication, retention, disk, network, page cache, request queues, consumer lag, processing latency, and recovery traffic.

codeBlocks.code:
Broker: request latency/errors, network, disk, JVM, under-replicated partitions
Controller: quorum health, elections, metadata operations
Producer: error/retry rate, batch size, compression, delivery latency
Consumer: records lag, time lag, poll/process/commit latency, rebalances
Streams/Connect: task state, restoration, DLQ/failure rate

callouts.title: Lag Is Not One Number
callouts.text: Offset lag lacks event age and processing health. Track time lag, throughput, partition skew, stuck consumers, and downstream completion.

subtopics.title: Failure, Upgrades & Production Checklist
subtopics.description: Automate partition reassignment carefully, preserve quorum and replica safety, test backup/restore of configuration and schemas, and perform supported rolling upgrades with compatibility review.

callouts.title: Production Checklist
callouts.text: Choose keys/partitions deliberately, require durable acknowledgements, make consumers idempotent, govern schemas, bound retries, secure every component, monitor lag and replica health, capacity-plan recovery, test broker/rack loss, and rehearse poison-event replay and upgrades.
